scope: Adversarial — find BranchScope bypass paths, missing UNIQUEs that allow duplication, FK omissions creating orphans, migration trail duplicates
approach: Hostile read-only analysis. Tried to find ways a malicious actor or buggy code could (a) bypass tenant isolation, (b) create duplicate records that violate business invariants, (c) leave orphan rows that grow forever, (d) silently corrupt fiscal evidence.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: bypass BranchScope via withoutGlobalScope from staff context
attack_attempts.method: BranchScope is applied as a global scope. Any caller can do `Model::withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class)`. Does the codebase protect against staff (non-admin) abuse?
evidence_read: app/Models/Scopes/BranchScope.php:27 — only Auth::check() gates the scope. The staff-branch enforcement is at line 39 (`where(field, '=', $userBranch)`).
attack_attempts.result: VERIFIED-PARTIAL — `withoutGlobalScope` is a Laravel API. The code base uses it intentionally (e.g., kiosk pre-auth lookups, fiscal cron, idempotency lookups). Any new caller adding it without thinking does bypass tenant isolation. There is no automated linter check. Tests cited (BranchScopeTest, IdempotencyBranchScopedTest) cover specific known callers but not the surface area.
attack_attempts.decision: STRUCTURAL-RECOMMENDATION — add a phpstan/PHPUnit sentinel that asserts `withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class)` calls are documented with `// [SCOPE-BYPASS-INTENT] reason` comment. Not a V1 blocker since prod path already audited.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: NFC card cloning cross-branch — Customer::where('nfc_uid')->first() returns wrong tenant customer
attack_attempts.method: Customer extends User. User exempted from BranchScope. nfc_uid is a column on `users`. If two branches use the same NFC tech and a card is cloned, lookups may return cross-tenant rows.
evidence_read: app/Models/Customer.php:23 — nfc_uid fillable, no scope
app/Models/User.php:90 — BranchScope applied to User but no-op due to instanceof guard in BranchScope.php:21
Migration 2026_04_20_220000_add_nfc_uid_to_customers.php — assumed adds nfc_uid column + index
attack_attempts.result: REAL-RISK — controller-level branch filtering is the only defense. There IS no UNIQUE(branch_id, nfc_uid) on users. Two branches CAN have the same nfc_uid value, and a lookup `Customer::where('nfc_uid', X)->first()` returns the first match deterministically by id, ignoring branch.
attack_attempts.removes_breaks: Adding UNIQUE(branch_id, nfc_uid) would break legitimate scenarios where one customer holds same card across branches. Adding UNIQUE(nfc_uid) globally would block legitimate parallel-use.
attack_attempts.decision: STRUCTURAL-RECOMMENDATION — audit all Customer::where('nfc_uid') callers (likely few, maybe 1-2 in loyalty controller) to ensure they always chain `->where('branch_id', $currentBranch)`. Add E2E test for this attack.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: orphan order_payments via FK cascade
attack_attempts.method: If Order is hard-deleted, do order_payments cascade or restrict?
evidence_read: database/migrations/2026_05_10_010000_secure_fiscal_audit_trail_immutability.php:85-95 — order_payments FK changed FROM cascadeOnDelete TO restrictOnDelete on order_id
Same file:131-141 — order_payments DELETE trigger fires SIGNAL 45000
attack_attempts.result: MITIGATED — hard DELETE of Order is now blocked by FK restrictOnDelete + order_payments DELETE trigger. Order soft-delete (SoftDeletes trait) does NOT fire FK or trigger — soft-delete is correct fiscal behavior (NF525 keeps the record).

attack_attempts.title: Attack: webhook double-processing via concurrent INSERT race
attack_attempts.method: Two requests with same Stripe event.id arrive simultaneously. Can they both process?
evidence_read: database/migrations/2026_05_09_120000_create_webhook_events_table.php:83 — UNIQUE(provider, webhook_id) named uk_webhook_provider_id
app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:18-28 — docblock prescribes firstOrCreate pattern
attack_attempts.result: MITIGATED at DB layer — even if both INSERTs race, only one wins via UNIQUE constraint. The losing INSERT throws QueryException which the handler catches, then re-reads the existing event. The docblock prescribes the correct pattern.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: forge fiscal sequence gap via concurrent allocation
attack_attempts.method: Two POS terminals close cash drawer at the exact same ms. Both try to allocate next fiscal_sequence_no.
evidence_read: database/migrations/2026_04_22_000001_add_fiscal_sequence_no_to_orders.php:37 — UNIQUE(branch_id, fiscal_sequence_no)
CLAUDE.md §8 — Cache::lock 5s + DB FOR UPDATE = triple defense (service-layer)
FiscalSequenceService is FROZEN per CLAUDE.md §7 — read-only mode
attack_attempts.result: MITIGATED — UNIQUE constraint rejects the loser. Service layer adds Cache::lock + FOR UPDATE. Triple defense.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: NF525 audit_logs row tampering via UPDATE
attack_attempts.method: Direct SQL UPDATE on audit_logs to alter prev_hash.
evidence_read: database/migrations/2026_04_22_000002_create_audit_logs_table.php:97-104 — MySQL trigger BEFORE UPDATE SIGNAL 45000
Same migration:121-126 — SQLite trigger BEFORE UPDATE RAISE ABORT
app/Models/AuditLog.php:45-50 — Eloquent updating() throws RuntimeException
attack_attempts.result: FULLY MITIGATED — trigger fires at DB layer even on raw SQL. Eloquent guard adds belt-and-braces.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: TRUNCATE bypass on audit_logs (known bypass)
attack_attempts.method: MySQL TRUNCATE does not fire BEFORE DELETE triggers. Can a DBA wipe fiscal evidence?
evidence_read: database/migrations/2026_04_22_000002_create_audit_logs_table.php:138-140 — commented 'TRUNCATE bypass mitigated via GRANT level (deploy doc)'
CLAUDE.md §8 — same caveat documented
attack_attempts.result: DOCUMENTED-MITIGATION — relies on production DB GRANT excluding TRUNCATE for app user. Cannot verify from code alone. RISK if deploy doc not followed.
attack_attempts.decision: URGENT-NF525-FLAG-DEPLOY — verify deploy docs strictly REVOKE TRUNCATE on audit_logs + z_reports + cash_movements + cash_drawer_sessions + order_payments + delivery_boy_cash_* for the app DB user. Owner-friendly framing: 'There is a known way to wipe the fiscal records via a low-level SQL command called TRUNCATE. The triggers do not block it. The protection is at the database-user-permission level. Need to verify deploy docs enforce REVOKE TRUNCATE on the app account.'

attack_attempts.title: Attack: race on idempotency_key — could same key submit twice and create 2 orders?
attack_attempts.method: If two simultaneous POSTs with same X-Idempotency-Key, does UNIQUE(branch_id, idempotency_key) reject the second?
evidence_read: database/migrations/2026_03_25_002938_add_idempotency_key_to_orders_table.php:17 — original UNIQUE(idempotency_key) GLOBAL
database/migrations/2026_04_18_140003_scope_idempotency_key_to_branch.php:35 — replaced with UNIQUE(branch_id, idempotency_key)
app/Services/Idempotency/IdempotencyKeyRepository.php:31 — atomic acquire() = SET NX EX equivalent via Cache::add()
app/Services/Idempotency/RedisIdempotencyKeyRepository.php:68 — Cache::add() documented atomic
attack_attempts.result: MITIGATED at TWO layers — Cache::add() lock + DB UNIQUE.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: same-timestamp migration ordering ambiguity
attack_attempts.method: ls shows 5 migrations sharing timestamp 2026_04_20_210000 / 2026_05_18_120000. Could ordering bug cause schema corruption?
evidence_read: ls database/migrations/2026_04_20_210000_* — 3 migrations: add_fiscal_identity_to_branches, create_printers_table, extend_dining_tables_occupancy
ls database/migrations/2026_05_18_120000_* — 2 migrations: add_webhook_events_order_id_fk, create_delivery_boy_cash_sessions_table
attack_attempts.result: LAW-MIGRATION-RUN-ORDER — Laravel runs migrations alphabetically WITHIN same timestamp. The 3 + 2 migrations are on distinct tables so order doesn't matter. No corruption risk.
attack_attempts.decision: ACCEPTABLE — naming convention quirk, not a bug.

attack_attempts.title: Attack: STI tables — Customer + User + admin all share `users` table
attack_attempts.method: Customer extends User. Admin role = same table. Can RBAC be bypassed via STI?
evidence_read: app/Models/Customer.php:9 — extends User
users table has nfc_uid + is_guest fillable (from Customer)
RBAC via Spatie permissions = separate model_has_roles table
attack_attempts.result: ACCEPTABLE — RBAC enforcement is at permission middleware, not at model-class layer. STI here is just a convention for 'this row represents an in-app customer'. Risk is low because all controllers check `tokenCan` or `permission:` middleware.

real_risks: RED-F1-002 (nfc_uid cross-branch lookup needs explicit filter)
RED-F1-007 (TRUNCATE bypass requires deploy doc verification)
summary.verdict: Data layer is hardened. Two findings require attention: NFC cross-branch lookup audit (controller-side, no schema change needed) and TRUNCATE deploy-doc verification. Neither is a code-blocker; both are operational/audit items.
